facts.claim: The most effective nature-based interventions were offered for between 8 and 12 weeks, and the optimal dose ranged from 20 to 90 min.
facts.quote: The most effective interventions were offered for between 8 and 12 weeks, and the optimal dose ranged from 20 to 90 min.

facts.claim: Positive associations between nature contact and health peaked between 200-300 minutes per week with no further gain.
facts.quote: Positive associations peaked between 200-300 mins per week with no further gain.

facts.claim: Residential greenness is linked to a statistically significant association with respiratory disease, low birth weight, cardiovascular disease, and other three diseases, except for allergic disease.
facts.quote: The meta-analysis result showed a statistically significant association between the residential greenness versus respiratory disease, low birth weight, cardiovascular disease, other three diseases, except for allergic disease.

facts.claim: Spending at least 120 minutes a week in nature is linked to a significantly greater likelihood of reporting good health and high well-being compared to no nature contact.
facts.quote: Compared to no nature contact last week, the likelihood of reporting good health or high well-being became significantly greater with contact ≥120 mins (e. g. 120-179 mins: ORs [95%CIs]: Health = 1. 59 [1. 31-1. 92]; Well-being = 1. 23 [1. 08-1. 40]).

facts.claim: Seven (78%) of the nine studies found a significant inverse relationship between an increase in surrounding greenness per 0·1 NDVI in a buffer zone of 500 m or less and the risk of all-cause mortality.
facts.quote: Seven (78%) of the nine studies found a significant inverse relationship between an increase in surrounding greenness per 0·1 NDVI in a buffer zone of 500 m or less and the risk of all-cause mortality

rejected.claim: Nature-based interventions were effective for improving depressive mood -0. 64 (95% CI: 1. 05 to -0. 23), reducing anxiety -0. 94 (95% CI: 0. 94 to -0. 01), improving positive affect 0. 95 (95% CI: 0. 59 to 1. 31), and reducing negative affect -0. 52 (95% CI: 0. 77 to -0. 26).
rejected.quote: Random effects meta-analysis of RCTs showed that NBIs were effective for improving depressive mood -0. 64 (95% CI: 1. 05 to -0. 23), reducing anxiety -0. 94 (95% CI: 0. 94 to -0. 01), improving positive affect 0. 95 (95% CI: 0. 59 to 1. 31), and reducing negative affect -0. 52 (95% CI: 0. 77 to -0. 26).

research.angle: While spending at least 120 minutes a week in nature is linked to better health and well-being, the most effective nature-based interventions for mental health may occur in doses of 20 to 90 minutes.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that regular nature contact and structured nature-based interventions are linked to improved mental and physical health outcomes, with specific benefits observed for disadvantaged groups.
research.caveat: The evidence for physical health improvements from nature-based interventions is less substantial than the evidence for mental health benefits.
